issue: Row rec/ck is labelled 'Book-side adjustment for check #2291 (enter + or −)', but the scorer cannot parse a leading '+': a student who follows the instruction and types '+360' is marked wrong (tolerance 0, answer 360).
evidence: src/lib/tbsScoring.ts parseAmount() strips $ , spaces, handles '-'/U+2212 and parentheses, then requires /^\d*\.?\d+$/. Running the same function under node: parseAmount('+360') = null, parseAmount('+ 360') = null, parseAmount('360') = 360. withinTolerance(null, 360, 0) = false, so the cell scores 0. The amountInputProps pattern in src/components/ui.tsx also has no '+' branch. The label is the only TBS row in content that says '(enter + or −)'.
fix: Content fix: relabel the row 'Book-side adjustment for check #2291 (enter a decrease as a negative number)' or 'Increase (decrease) to book balance for check #2291'. Code fix (app owners): let parseAmount accept a leading '+' (strip it before the digit test) and add it to the input pattern.

issue: Part cl row 'net' (Net accounts receivable, answer 544,050) depends on an assumption that appears only in the explanation: that the $1,200 NSF check reinstated in the bank-reconciliation entry is already included in the 12/31 aging. The exhibits never say so, and the more natural reading is the opposite.
evidence: Key: 570,000 − 25,950 = 544,050; explanation adds '(The NSF check reinstated in the bank reconciliation is assumed to be already reflected in the aging.)'. But the NSF check is a book-side reconciling item, i.e. by definition not yet recorded in Summit's books, and the student's own JE in part je debits Accounts receivable 1,200. A student who carries that entry into AR gets 571,200 − 25,950 = 545,250 (or a different allowance if they age the 1,200). With tolerance 0 that defensible answer scores wrong, and the required-allowance row is also affected under that reading.
source: ASC 326-20-30 (allowance on amortized-cost receivables); internal consistency of the TBS exhibits
fix: Add to the aging exhibit: 'The aging was prepared after recording the bank-reconciliation adjustments and includes the $1,200 NSF receivable (Current bucket).' Alternatively, state 'Ignore the NSF check for the aging'. Keep the explanation note consistent with whichever fact is added.

issue: Stem begins 'Using the previous facts…' and does not restate the adjusted book balance it depends on (far-cash-12). Practice sets are shuffled, so the student usually sees this item without far-cash-12; the stem then lacks the fact needed to answer.
evidence: src/lib/quiz.ts buildQuiz(): eligible items are shuffle()d and re-ordered by attempts, and buildMasteryCheck() also shuffles; nothing keeps far-cash-12 immediately before far-cash-13. Without 12's facts the stem gives only bank 22,300 and DIT 3,000, so outstanding checks (key 3,840 = 22,300 + 3,000 − 21,460) cannot be computed.
source: src/lib/quiz.ts; item-writing standard (stem complete and self-contained)
fix: Make the stem self-contained: 'The adjusted (correct) book balance is $21,460. The bank statement balance is $22,300 and deposits in transit are $3,000. What are the outstanding checks?' or restate far-cash-12's facts in full.

issue: Lesson–item alignment: about a third of the practice items test rules the lesson never teaches, including classic exam topics (imprest petty cash, unmailed checks at year-end).
evidence: Untaught in the lesson body or takeaways: imprest petty cash replenishment and cash short/over (far-cash-11, -17, -25); checks written and recorded but held/unmailed at year-end are added back to cash and AP (far-cash-19); foreign-currency cash measured at the year-end rate (far-cash-20); roll-forward of outstanding checks and deposits in transit, i.e. proof-of-cash logic (far-cash-26, -27); current vs noncurrent classification of a legally restricted compensating balance by the term of the related loan (far-cash-05, -24 — the lesson says only 'reported separately'). Overdraft presentation (far-cash-04, -15) appears only as a key takeaway, never in the body. 9–11 of 28 practice items are affected.
source: Blueprint FAR-II.A tasks (review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv rows FAR-II.A.1–A.4); ASC 210-10-45-4; SEC Reg S-X 5-02.1 / ASC 210-10-S99-2
fix: Add a short 'Other cash issues' section: (1) imprest petty cash: establishment, replenishment entry (Dr expenses, Dr/Cr cash short and over, Cr Cash), period-end treatment; (2) unmailed/postdated outgoing checks (window dressing): reverse to Cash and AP; (3) compensating balances: legally restricted → separate line, current if the borrowing is short-term, noncurrent if long-term; not legally restricted → disclose; (4) overdrafts: current liability, offset only with a right of setoff at the same bank; (5) rolling DIT/outstanding checks forward (beginning + book − bank). Mark the foreign-currency item optional or move it (see the separate finding).
